title: The IRS called and wants a gift card? Myth vs fact
label: Tax myth vs fact

hook.sub: AI voices make it sound real. Here's the tell.

items.l: IRS calls first about a bill
Pay by gift card or wire
A letter comes in the mail first

beats.text: Can you question the amount before you pay?
The IRS gives you a chance to *appeal.*
beats.sub: No demand for payment on the spot.

beats.text: Hang up. Check your *IRS online account.*

cta.sub: We'll DM you our AI and tax safety guide.

captions.instagram:
With AI voices, a fake IRS call can sound very real. The rules for spotting one haven't changed.

✔️ The IRS usually starts with a letter in the mail. Even before a call or visit, you generally get several notices first.
✔️ The IRS doesn't demand immediate payment by prepaid debit card, gift card or wire transfer.
✔️ It doesn't threaten arrest by local police, and it lets you question or appeal what you owe.
✔️ Not sure? Hang up and look at your IRS online account. Report IRS-looking emails to phishing@irs.gov.

Save this for the next time someone in your family gets that call.

Source: IRS, How to know it's really the IRS.
